questions.question: A sum amounts to ₹6,600 in 2 years and ₹7,200 in 4 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.questionHtml: A sum amounts to ₹6,600 in 2 years and ₹7,200 in 4 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
SI for 2 years (from year 2 to year 4) = 7200 − 6600 = ₹600 → SI per year = ₹300.

Principal = 6600 − 2 × 300 = 6000.

Rate = (300 / 6000) × 100 = 5%.

questions.question: A kite is soaring at an altitude of 75 meters above the ground, with its string temporarily secured to a point on the ground. The angle of elevation of the string relative to the ground is 30 degrees. Given that the string remains taut, what is the length of the string?
questions.questionHtml: A kite is soaring at an altitude of 75 meters above the ground, with its string temporarily secured to a point on the ground. The angle of elevation of the string relative to the ground is 30 degrees. Given that the string remains taut, what is the length of the string?
questions.solution:
Let L = string length.

sin 30° = altitude / L → 1/2 = 75 / L → L = 150 m.

questions.question: A rectangular fish tank with a base of 100 cm × 50 cm contains water up to a height of 20 cm. If 5 identical spherical stones, each with a radius of 5 cm, are dropped into the tank and fully submerged, what is the rise in the water level?
questions.questionHtml: A rectangular fish tank with a base of 100 cm × 50 cm contains water up to a height of 20 cm. If 5 identical spherical stones, each with a radius of 5 cm, are dropped into the tank and fully submerged, what is the rise in the water level?
questions.solution:
Volume of one sphere = (4/3)π(5)³ = 500π/3 cm³.

For 5 spheres = 2500π/3 cm³.

Base area = 100 × 50 = 5000 cm².

Rise = volume / base = (2500π/3) / 5000 = π/6 cm.

questions.questionHtml: A 50-liter solution contains acid and water in the ratio 3:2. How much water must be added to make the ratio 1:1?
questions.solution:
Acid = 3/5 × 50 = 30 L. Water = 50 − 30 = 20 L.

Let x L water added.

For 1:1 → acid = water → 30 = 20 + x → x = 10 L.

questions.question: If 10 men or 15 women can complete a work in 170 days, how long will 20 men and 20 women take for completing the same work?
questions.questionHtml: If 10 men or 15 women can complete a work in 170 days, how long will 20 men and 20 women take for completing the same work?
questions.solution:
10 men = 15 women → 1 man = 1.5 women.

Work = 15 × 170 = 2550 woman-days.

20 men = 30 women. 20 men + 20 women = 50 women.

Time = 2550 / 50 = 51 days.

questions.question: A student took 7 tests and had an average of 72. If his average after 8 tests increased to 73, what was his score on the 8th test?
questions.questionHtml: A student took 7 tests and had an average of 72. If his average after 8 tests increased to 73, what was his score on the 8th test?
questions.solution:
Total of 7 tests = 7 × 72 = 504.

Total of 8 tests = 8 × 73 = 584.

8th test score = 584 − 504 = 80.

questions.question: A solution of 100 litres has a 60% salt concentration. How many litres of water must be added to reduce the concentration to 40%, and then how much pure salt must be added to bring the concentration back to 50%?
questions.questionHtml: A solution of 100 litres has a 60% salt concentration. How many litres of water must be added to reduce the concentration to 40%, and then how much pure salt must be added to bring the concentration back to 50%?

options.text: Add 50 L of water, then 30 L of salt
options.html: Add 50 L of water, then 30 L of salt

options.text: Add 90 L of water, then 70 L of salt
options.html: Add 90 L of water, then 70 L of salt

options.text: Add 70 L of water, then 30 L of salt
options.html: Add 70 L of water, then 30 L of salt

options.text: Add 50 L of water, then 10 L of salt
options.html: Add 50 L of water, then 10 L of salt

questions.solution:
Initial salt = 60 L (60% of 100 L).

Add w L water → 60/(100 + w) = 0.40 → w = 50 L.

New total = 150 L with 60 L salt.

Add s L pure salt → (60 + s)/(150 + s) = 0.50 → 60 + s = 75 + 0.5s → 0.5s = 15 → s = 30 L.

questions.question: If sin A = 4/5 and A lies in 2nd quadrant, find the value of (1 + tan A)(1 − tan A).
questions.questionHtml: If sin A = 4/5 and A lies in 2nd quadrant, find the value of (1 + tan A)(1 − tan A).
questions.solution:
(1 + tanA)(1 − tanA) = 1 − tan²A.

In 2nd quadrant, cosA = −3/5; tanA = sinA/cosA = (4/5)/(−3/5) = −4/3.

1 − tan²A = 1 − 16/9 = −7/9.

options.text: On one of the sides of the triangle.
options.html: On one of the sides of the triangle.

options.text: At one of the vertices of the triangle.
options.html: At one of the vertices of the triangle.

questions.solution:
For an obtuse triangle, two of the altitudes intersect outside the triangle.

Hence the orthocenter lies outside the triangle, on the opposite side of the obtuse angle.

questions.question: A point P is outside a circle. The length of the tangent from P is 10 cm, and the distance from P to the center is √125 cm. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.questionHtml: A point P is outside a circle. The length of the tangent from P is 10 cm, and the distance from P to the center is √125 cm. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution:
OP² = r² + tangent².

125 = r² + 100 → r² = 25 → r = 5 cm.
